_meta.scope: Registry of all characters: unique CHAR-* ID, aliases, tier, layer, faction, appearances, render_mode. Per-character details go under characters/<CHAR-id>/ (appearance.json, personality.json, dialogue_style.json, voice.json, ...). How each speaking figure is realised on screen follows cultivation.json as amended by BIB-0027 (user ruling 2026-09-22, brief.md 'Realistic fantasy film adapted from a fairy tale'): speaking animals are photoreal CGI animals integrated into live-action plates, wearing only the iconic period props the text gives them (SUP-002); the Gryphon and the Mock Turtle are photoreal CGI fantastical creatures (SUP-010); the Frog-Footman and Fish-Footman are CGI frog-/fish-bodied figures in livery whose exact anatomy is flagged pending_H2 (04-creatures/creature with 03-characters/appearance); card figures and human dream-figures stay human performers in 1862 dress, unchanged (SUP-004). Every one of these figures is registered here as CHAR-*, never in creatures/, with a render_mode field recording the realisation.

layer_enum.waking: appears only in the 1862 riverbank/family/farm frame (ev0001, ev0053-ev0054)
layer_enum.dream: appears only inside Alice's dream (ev0002-ev0052); realised per SUP-002/SUP-010/SUP-004 as amended by BIB-0027 — a photoreal CGI animal or fantastical creature if an animal/creature figure, a human performer in 1862 dress if a card or human figure — see each entry's render_mode and performer_concept
layer_enum.both: the same person, as themselves, appears in both layers (Alice only — she is both the waking girl and the dreamer's presence throughout her own dream)
layer_enum.both-echo: H1 ruling 5.3 B light doubling: a waking-layer person is echoed by a distinct dream-layer figure/reference (housemaid → Mary Ann mention; sister → glimpsed at the trial). The dream side of the Dinah → Cheshire Cat echo is out of scope here: Dinah is spoken of only (TERM-0025), never shown on screen, and has no registry id (bible/creatures/creature.json _meta.zero_entries_considered_and_excluded); CHAR-cheshire-cat itself is a pure 'dream' layer entry that cross-references the echo in its doubling field.

render_mode_enum.human_performer: live human actor in costume — SUP-004 card figures, human dream-figures (Hatter, Duchess, Cook, executioner, Pat, crowds of officers/soldiers/courtiers), and waking-frame humans; unchanged by BIB-0027
render_mode_enum.cgi_animal: photoreal CGI animal composited into live-action plates: naturalistic anatomy, fur/feather/scale/shell detail, real weight and light, only the minimal iconic period props the text gives it, no cartoon face, no human in animal costume (SUP-002, amended BIB-0027; the Frog-/Fish-Footmen anatomy is flagged pending_H2)
render_mode_enum.cgi_fantastical: photoreal CGI fantastical creature with no single real-world species referent (SUP-010, amended BIB-0027): the Gryphon (griffin) and the Mock Turtle (calf-headed turtle)

characters[].name: canonical production name
characters[].original_name: name/description as it appears in the source text, or null if wholly designed
characters[].age: designed working value or null (not applicable to non-human dream figures)
characters[].performer_concept: for dream/both-echo entries only: one-line design concept matching render_mode — a SUP-002/SUP-010 photoreal-CGI concept for cgi_animal/cgi_fantastical figures, or a SUP-004/human-figure 1862-dress concept for human_performer figures (BIB-0027); concept-level only, full visual spec is owned by 03-characters/appearance, 04-creatures/creature (CGI figures) and 06-art/costume
characters[].render_mode: human_performer|cgi_animal|cgi_fantastical (added BIB-0027): how this figure is realised on screen; see render_mode_enum
characters[].doubling: null, or a note + ref describing the H1 5.3 B echo relationship this entry participates in

_meta.scope_note: Registers every speaking or on-screen entity found in story/structured_story (all chapter shards) and story/events.json, plus every CHAR-* slug reserved in bible/_index.json forward_refs_pending (25 ids, honoured verbatim). Purely off-screen real-world/recitation name-drops that never appear as dream-figures or waking participants (e.g. Mabel, Ada, William the Conqueror, Father William, Elsie/Lacie/Tillie, Queen Victoria — all already covered as plain terms in dictionary.json) are excluded from this character registry, EXCEPT CHAR-tortoise, which forward_refs_pending explicitly mandates even though the Tortoise is told-only and never depicted on screen (see its entry's notes).

amendments.authority: User ruling in chat, 2026-09-22 (bible/changelog.md BIB-0027; qa/defects/DEF-p4-style-001 a = B): "会说话的角色可以用CGI动物，因为影片应该是写实奇幻风格；另外环境加入穆夏绘画的风格". Supersedes the H1 5.1 A human-performer-for-every-speaking-figure reading. Species list and Frog-/Fish-Footman anatomy are the workflow-orchestrator's scope interpretation, re-surfaced at H2.
entries_changed: performer_concept text for every CGI-rendered entry (cgi_animal / cgi_fantastical)
amendments.entries_unchanged_by_design: SUP-004 card figures (King/Queen/Knave, gardeners, soldiers, courtiers) and human dream-figures (Hatter, Duchess, Cook, executioner, Pat, officer/crowd ensembles) stay render_mode human_performer, performer_concept text unchanged. CHAR-duchess-baby stays render_mode human_performer per SUP-006 (unamended); only its pig end-state CGI treatment is an open question, flagged pending_H2 (see disambiguation).

characters.name: Alice

first_appearance.quote: Alice was beginning to get very tired of sitting by her sister on the bank

characters.disambiguation: Not to be confused with CHAR-family-housemaid: the White Rabbit mistakes Alice for his housemaid Mary Ann in ch004, but Mary Ann is a separate, never-seen dream figure (TERM-0010) doubling the family's real housemaid, not an alias of Alice.
characters.reason: Protagonist and sole dreamer: present as herself in the waking frame (ch001, ch012) and, per SUP-001, present throughout the dream as the dreaming consciousness experiencing it (ch002-ch011), hence layer 'both' rather than 'dream'. Age: the source never gives a number; world.json fixed 'about ten' as a world-level working value at H1 (h1_summary.md section 1, ruling 5.6 A) and explicitly left the final age to 03-characters to confirm, which this entry does. Note: bible/dictionary.json TERM-0001 still describes her as 'seven-year-old', a pre-H1 draft characterization that conflicts with the confirmed H1 age; filed as DEF-p3-dictionary-001 for memory-bible/dictionary to reconcile, not corrected here.
characters.notes: Chapter span ev0001-ev0054 per story_timeline.json; the only character present in literally every chapter.

characters.name: Alice's Sister

doubling.echoed_as: a spectator glimpsed at the trial in the dream (ch012)
doubling.note: The only one of the three H1 5.3 B doublings where the same actor plays herself (lightly re-dressed as a court spectator) rather than a differently-named dream figure; hence layer 'both-echo' rather than a separate CHAR id.

first_appearance.quote: sitting by her sister on the bank, and of having nothing to do

characters.reason: Never named in the source; 'mid-teens' follows h1_summary.md section 1 (ruling 5.6 A, 'sister glimpsed at the trial') and world.json frame.social_class ('an older sister free to read on a weekday afternoon'). The trial-glimpse appearance is a designed staging beat realizing ruling 5.3 B, not stated verbatim in ch011-012; it is inferred but load-bearing for the dream's closing return to the bank.

characters.name: The Family Housemaid
characters.performer_concept: Never depicted on screen in either layer; if a waking-frame glimpse is staged, plain 1862 domestic-servant dress, no animal/card coding needed (she is not a dream-figure herself, only referenced from within the dream).

doubling.echoed_as: 'Mary Ann', the White Rabbit's off-page housemaid he mistakes Alice for

first_appearance.quote: Why, Mary Ann, what _are_ you doing out here?

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from CHAR-alice (whom the White Rabbit mistakes for Mary Ann) and from the dream's own unseen 'Mary Ann' as a name-only reference (TERM-0010); this entry is the waking-world person that reference echoes per ruling 5.3 B.
characters.reason: The housemaid's existence is inferred from world.json frame.social_class ('at least one housemaid') and TERM-0147, which is itself inferred from the dream's 'Mary Ann' reference (ch004) and the class markers in ch002/ch009. She is never shown or named directly in the waking frame; she is registered here (rather than left unregistered) because ruling 5.3 B and the dictionary (TERM-0010, TERM-0147) both treat her as the specific real-world anchor for the Mary Ann reference, and 'alias_unambiguous' requires 'Mary Ann' to resolve to one clear entity rather than floating unattached.

characters.name: White Rabbit
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI rabbit (BIB-0027, SUP-002) composited into live-action plates: naturalistic anatomy, fur detail, pink eyes, real weight and light; wears only the text's iconic props made to 1862 patterns — a fussy waistcoat, white kid gloves and a large pocket watch worked into a constant checking-the-time tic; no cartoon face, no human in animal costume.

first_appearance.quote: suddenly a White Rabbit with pink eyes ran close by her

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from the real, silent white rabbit of the waking frame (a genuine on-screen animal, per SUP-002 and world.json wonderland_real_counterparts key cp-rabbit-hole), which is registered by 04-creatures/creature, not here. Per H1 ruling 5.3 B / P-012, this dream character is not one of the three declared light-doublings; it is its own dream-figure, not an official echo of the waking rabbit.

characters.name: Queen of Hearts
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in a flat, heavily card-suited crimson gown/tabard (per FAC-house-of-hearts emblem_visual) with an oversized enamelled heart device and a stylised crown; blocking and posture read as a flat playing-card figure per SUP-004.

first_appearance.quote: last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS

characters.notes: Per SUP-014, her constant beheading sentences are staged as bluster never carried out; see cultivation.json SUP-014.

characters.name: King of Hearts
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in flat card-suited livery echoing the Queen's crimson/heart devices, crown worn awkwardly over a judge's wig at the trial (ch011), per FAC-house-of-hearts emblem_visual.

first_appearance.quote: last of all this grand procession, came THE KING AND QUEEN OF HEARTS

characters.name: The Duchess
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in plain, visibly poorer gentry dress than the Hearts court's card livery (per FAC-duchess-household emblem_visual); no animal coding, since she is textually human in the source, not an animal figure.

first_appearance.quote: the Duchess was sitting on a three-legged stool in the middle, nursing a baby

characters.name: The Hatter
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in an oversized hat still bearing its price-tag ('In this style 10/6'), otherwise full 1862 dress; no literal animal, since the Hatter is textually human, but plays broad, twitchy, over-caffeinated physical comedy as his character-coded touch.

first_appearance.quote: In _that_ direction,” the Cat said, waving its right paw round, “lives a Hatter

characters.notes: First witness called at the trial (ch011); asks Alice the unanswered riddle 'Why is a raven like a writing-desk?' (TERM-0119).

characters.name: Cheshire Cat
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI cat (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic tabby-toned fur, anatomy, weight and light, a fixed exaggerated grin and silent catlike stillness; no cartoon face, no human in cat costume. The vanish-to-grin beat (SUP-005) is executed as a photographic dissolve on the CGI figure, not a costume trick.

doubling.echoes: Dinah, Alice's real waking-world pet cat
doubling.note: Dinah is spoken of only (TERM-0025), never shown on screen, and has no registry id (bible/creatures/creature.json _meta.zero_entries_considered_and_excluded). This entry carries the dream-side half of the echo.

first_appearance.quote: she was a little startled by seeing the Cheshire Cat sitting on a bough of a tree

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from Dinah (TERM-0025); the two are linked only by the H1 5.3 B doubling ruling, not the same registry entry.
characters.reason: Source uses "it"; female follows H1 5.3 B doubling with Dinah ("she", ch002-p22).

characters.name: March Hare
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI hare (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic anatomy, fur and long ears, real weight and light, a twitchy nose tic; no cartoon face, no human in hare costume.

first_appearance.quote: in _that_ direction,” waving the other paw, “lives a March Hare

characters.name: The Dormouse
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI dormouse (BIB-0027, SUP-002): small-framed, naturalistic soft grey/brown fur, anatomy and weight, perpetually drowsy, a curled, nested sleeping posture used as a living cushion between the Hatter and March Hare; no cartoon face, no human in rodent costume.

first_appearance.quote: a Dormouse was sitting between them, fast asleep

characters.reason: Gender 'male' per source: ch007-p66, "The Dormouse slowly opened his eyes. 'I wasn't asleep,' he said" (not inferred).
characters.notes: Tells the treacle-well story of Elsie, Lacie and Tillie (ch007); those three are a told-only story-within-the-story and are not registered as characters (see _meta.scope_note).

characters.name: The Mouse
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI mouse (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic grey fur, anatomy and whiskers, real weight and light, damp-looking after swimming the pool of tears, a startled, bristling reaction tic; no cartoon face, no human in rodent costume.

first_appearance.quote: she soon made out that it was only a mouse that had slipped in like herself

characters.reason: Gender 'male' per source: ch002-p23, "cried the Mouse, who was trembling down to the end of his tail" (not inferred).
characters.notes: Leads the Caucus-race company off in fright (CUL-044) after Alice mentions Dinah; does not reappear after ch003.

characters.name: The Cook
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002, plain kitchen dress, no animal coding (textually human); character-coded by pepper-throwing, pan-hurling temper and a pepper-box carried into the courtroom.

first_appearance.quote: the cook was leaning over the fire, stirring a large cauldron

characters.name: Bill
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI lizard (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic scaled skin, anatomy and a lean, sinuous posture, real weight and light; sent down a chimney and later seated in the jury-box with a squeaking pencil; no cartoon face, no human in lizard costume.

first_appearance.quote: “This is Bill,” she gave one sharp kick

characters.notes: The only named individual among the twelve jurors of OFF-007; the rest of the jury is registered as CHAR-jury-ensemble.

characters.name: Knave of Hearts
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in flat card-suited page livery (per FAC-house-of-hearts emblem_visual, a Jack device), carrying the King's crown on a cushion in procession, then in chains as the trial's defendant.

first_appearance.quote: Then followed the Knave of Hearts, carrying the King’s crown on a crimson velvet cushion

characters.notes: Sole formally accused defendant in the story; the trial is interrupted before a verdict (story/events.json broken_chains, ev0052).

characters.name: The Gryphon
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI fantastical creature (BIB-0027, SUP-010): the classical griffin — eagle head, wings and forelegs; lion hindquarters and tail — naturalistic feather and fur, real weight and light; no cartoon styling, no human in partial costume; sent by the Queen to escort Alice.

first_appearance.quote: They very soon came upon a Gryphon, lying fast asleep in the sun

characters.notes: States the Queen never actually executes anyone ('it's all her fancy', ch009), the key source line behind SUP-014.

characters.name: The Mock Turtle
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI fantastical creature (BIB-0027, SUP-010): a turtle-bodied creature carrying the calf's head, hind hooves and tail conventionally associated with 'mock turtle soup' (the source's own visual pun made flesh), naturalistic shell, hide and hoof detail, real weight and light; no cartoon styling, no human in partial costume; a sobbing, sighing vocal tic.

first_appearance.quote: “It’s the thing Mock Turtle Soup is made from,” said the Queen

characters.notes: Former pupil of CHAR-tortoise's undersea school (FAC-school-in-the-sea, told only, ch009-ch010).

characters.name: The Tortoise
characters.performer_concept: Told-only figure; if ever visualized (e.g. in a stylised flashback insert), a photoreal CGI tortoise per SUP-002 (BIB-0027): naturalistic shell and anatomy, slow deliberate movement; no cartoon face, no human in tortoise costume.

first_appearance.quote: The master was an old Turtle—we used to call him Tortoise

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from CHAR-mock-turtle: 'Tortoise' is the Mock Turtle's old schoolmaster, nicknamed Tortoise as a pun ('he taught us'), never itself a tortoise by species and never appearing on screen — a told-only anecdote within the Mock Turtle's own dialogue.
characters.notes: Registered because bible/_index.json forward_refs_pending mandates this exact slug even though the character is mentioned-only and never depicted in person; kept at tier 'extra' and layer 'dream' (an anecdote told inside the dream) to reflect that.

characters.name: The Caterpillar
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI caterpillar (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic blue-toned segmented anatomy, real weight and light, seated atop a mushroom prop, smoking a hookah — the text's one iconic prop; no cartoon face, no human in insect costume.

first_appearance.quote: her eyes immediately met those of a large blue caterpillar

characters.notes: Dictionary TERM-0037 cites first_seen chapter ch004; structured_story places the scene in ch005 ('Advice from a Caterpillar', per story/chapter_manifest.json), which this entry follows as the authoritative chapter source per WRITE_RULES.md section 2.

characters.name: The Pigeon
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI pigeon (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic feather detail and anatomy, real weight and light, agitated wing movements, protective/aggressive posture defending an unseen nest; no cartoon face, no human in bird costume.

first_appearance.quote: a large pigeon had flown into her face

characters.name: Duck
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI duck (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic feather and bill anatomy, real weight and light, fresh out of the pool of tears; no cartoon face, no human in bird costume.

first_appearance.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet

characters.reason: The source calls the Duck 'it'. His one intervention is a pedantic question about what the Archbishop of Canterbury 'found' (ch003) — a churchy, literal-minded young gentleman; male gives the party a balanced mix alongside the female Lory, Eaglet, Canary and Crabs.
characters.notes: Interrupts the Mouse's dry recitation to ask what the archbishop 'found' (ch003).

characters.name: Lory
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI lory parrot (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic bright plumage and anatomy, real weight and light, a prim, argumentative manner; no cartoon face, no human in bird costume.

first_appearance.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet

characters.reason: The source calls the Lory 'it'. She argues with Alice as the elder who 'must know better' and turns sulky (ch003-p02) — the bossy older-girl dynamic; a prim young woman fits it and balances the party.

characters.name: Eaglet
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI eaglet (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic downy fledgling plumage and anatomy, real weight and light; no cartoon face, no human in bird costume.

first_appearance.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet

characters.reason: The source calls the Eaglet 'it'. A cheeky young fledgling who mocks the Dodo's long words and hides a smile (ch003-p15); played as a younger girl, the party's youngest, balancing the Lory as the elder.

characters.name: The Dodo
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI dodo (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic stout-bodied anatomy, plumage and large beak, real weight and light, fond of long words; no cartoon face, no human in bird costume.

first_appearance.quote: there were a Duck and a Dodo, a Lory and an Eaglet

characters.notes: Leads FAC-caucus-race-company; proposes and organizes the Caucus-race, declares 'everybody has won', and gives Alice her own thimble as a prize.

characters.name: Canary
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI canary (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic bright yellow-toned plumage and anatomy, real weight and light, a small bird-call vocal tic, part of the Caucus-race party; no cartoon face, no human in bird costume.

first_appearance.quote: Silence all round, if you please!

characters.reason: The source says 'it'; a parent gathering and bedding her brood (ch003-p47, "a Canary called out in a trembling voice to its children, 'Come away, my dears! It's high time you were all in bed!'") is played as a mother.

characters.name: Magpie
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI magpie (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic black-and-white plumage and anatomy, real weight and light, wrapping up carefully as a pretext to leave; no cartoon face, no human in bird costume.

first_appearance.quote: one old Magpie began wrapping itself up very carefully, remarking, “I really must be getting home; the night-air doesn’t suit my throat!”

characters.reason: The source says only 'one old Magpie' ('it'). A fussy old hypochondriac gentleman muffling his throat against the night air; male balances the party (the other bank speakers who leave in this beat — the Canary and the Crabs — are female).

characters.name: Old Crab
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI crab (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic shell and anatomy, real weight and light, a sidling gait, part of the Caucus-race party; no cartoon face, no human in crustacean costume.

first_appearance.quote: Silence all round, if you please!

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from CHAR-young-crab: paired in the source as an elder scolding a youngster, not the same individual.
characters.reason: Gender 'female' per source: ch003-p43, "an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter" (mother and daughter; not inferred).

characters.name: Young Crab
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI crab (BIB-0027, SUP-002): naturalistic shell and anatomy, real weight and light, a sidling gait, part of the Caucus-race party; no cartoon face, no human in crustacean costume.

first_appearance.quote: Silence all round, if you please!

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from CHAR-old-crab: the one scolded by its elder in the source, not the same individual.
characters.reason: Gender 'female' per source: ch003-p43, "an old Crab took the opportunity of saying to her daughter" (mother and daughter; not inferred).

characters.name: Fish-Footman
characters.performer_concept: CGI fish-bodied figure in crown livery (BIB-0027, SUP-002/XA-magic-02): naturalistic scale and fin detail, real weight and light, delivers the Queen's croquet invitation; how far the anatomy is humanised to wear/handle livery is owned by 04-creatures/creature with 03-characters/appearance and is flagged pending_H2.

first_appearance.quote: a footman in livery came running out of the wood

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from CHAR-frog-footman: they appear in the same single scene as a paired hand-off, not the same individual.

characters.name: Frog-Footman
characters.performer_concept: CGI frog-bodied figure in the Duchess household's plain, faded livery (BIB-0027, SUP-002/XA-magic-02; FAC-duchess-household emblem_visual): naturalistic skin, large bulging-eyed anatomy, real weight and light, sits uselessly by the Duchess's door; how far the anatomy is humanised to wear/handle livery is owned by 04-creatures/creature with 03-characters/appearance and is flagged pending_H2.

first_appearance.quote: another footman in livery, with a round face, and large eyes like a frog

characters.disambiguation: Distinct from CHAR-fish-footman: they appear in the same single scene as a paired hand-off, not the same individual.
characters.reason: Re-pointed from FAC-house-of-hearts to FAC-duchess-household: the source has him open the Duchess's door and receive the Queen's invitation on her behalf (ch006-p01, ch006-p02), and locked FREL-001 models a crown-to-Duchess-household hand-off. Per DEF-p3-appearance-303-a and DEF-p3-relationship-001-a.

characters.name: Gardener Two
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in flat card-suited gardening livery per FAC-house-of-hearts emblem_visual, with a numeral 'Two' rank device; the card is the Two of SPADES (BIB-0029, DEF-p4-char-301: the club suit belongs to the card soldiers and the visiting Clubs monarchs), read as oblong and flat, hands/feet at the corners.

first_appearance.quote: Two began in a low voice, “Why the fact is, you see, Miss

characters.disambiguation: One of three named gardeners (with CHAR-gardener-five, CHAR-gardener-seven); unnamed additional gardening staff are registered separately as CHAR-royal-gardeners-ensemble.
characters.notes: Explains to Alice that a white rose-tree was planted where a red one should have been.

characters.name: Gardener Five
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in flat card-suited gardening livery per FAC-house-of-hearts emblem_visual, with a numeral 'Five' rank device; the card is the Five of SPADES (BIB-0029).

first_appearance.quote: “I couldn’t help it,” said Five, in a sulky tone; “Seven jogged my elbow.”

characters.disambiguation: One of three named gardeners (with CHAR-gardener-two, CHAR-gardener-seven).
characters.notes: Blames CHAR-gardener-seven for jogging his elbow, sparking the roses' misprint of red paint.

characters.name: Gardener Seven
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in flat card-suited gardening livery per FAC-house-of-hearts emblem_visual, with a numeral 'Seven' rank device; the card is the Seven of SPADES (BIB-0029).

first_appearance.quote: On which Seven looked up and said, “That’s right, Five!

characters.disambiguation: One of three named gardeners (with CHAR-gardener-two, CHAR-gardener-five).

characters.name: Pat
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002, no species specified in the source; plain 1862 outdoor-gardening dress, no animal coding, distinguished by an Irish idiom ('yer honour').

first_appearance.quote: Sure then I’m here! Digging for apples, yer honour!

characters.notes: White Rabbit's outdoor helper, found 'digging for apples' (TERM-0024); species not specified in the text.

characters.name: The Royal Executioner
characters.performer_concept: Human performer per SUP-002 in crown livery, no animal coding; the office reads from livery and a pushed-back black hood only. No axe, block or other execution device is ever shown (SUP-014).

first_appearance.quote: there was a dispute going on between the executioner, the King, and the Queen

characters.notes: Argues that a head cannot be cut off without a body attached, in the farcical Cheshire Cat beheading dispute (SUP-005); never completes a beheading on-page.

characters.name: The Jury
characters.performer_concept: Photoreal CGI animal jurors (BIB-0027, SUP-002) seated in the jury-box, an assortment of guinea-pigs, birds and other small creatures per the source's 'all writing on slates'; naturalistic anatomy and texture, no cartoon faces, no humans in animal costume; no individual identity beyond CHAR-bill-the-lizard, who is registered separately.

first_appearance.quote: the twelve jurors were all writing very busily on slates

characters.disambiguation: Ensemble/crowd entry for the eleven unnamed jurors; CHAR-bill-the-lizard is the twelfth, individually named juror and is registered separately, not duplicated here.
characters.reason: Registered as a group entry per the work order's instruction to include jury/soldiers/gardeners/Caucus-race-party crowd entities; individual jurors beyond Bill are never named or individually distinguished in the source. Gender 'male' is sourced, not inferred: the source calls them 'jury-men' (ch011-p04) / 'jurymen' (ch012-p01); English juries in 1862 were all-male, so all eleven are male (gender_mix male 11 / female 0).
